A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARM-FM research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding algorithms, experiments, figures, tables and reward-machine listings can be matched despite reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments, component ablations, zero-shot demonstrations and foundation-model generation evaluations in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally documents qualitative generation failures and human corrections in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The generator–critic construction, optional human verification, language-conditioned policy, combined rewards and Algorithm 1 are retained. Appendix A.4 elaborates the existing human-feedback step; the additional labeling code implements terminal events already present in v1's reward machine.

E1.justification: The evaluated MiniGrid/BabyAI, Craftium, Meta-World and XLand-MiniGrid coverage is retained, including procedural layouts and compositional generalization. The new human-intervention discussion does not establish additional evaluated tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained across the main and appendix experiments. Figures 6–7 relabel the existing 'LLM Agent' curves as 'ReAct'; the new related-work table provides conceptual comparisons, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Task selections, training budgets, evaluation metrics and RL hyperparameters remain unchanged, including v1 Tables 3–6 matched to v3 Tables 5–8. Naming GPT-4o and describing human corrections disclose existing experimental details rather than establish revised settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4/Table 3 adds qualitative failure-and-correction cases involving missing key-loss transitions, overly sparse KeyCorridor rewards and Meta-World local optima. Existing component ablations, extended-training checks, embedding analysis and CLIP failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three independent random seeds with one-standard-deviation shading or error bars. The listed task seeds are unchanged, and no new statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Benchmark curves, generation-correctness results and zero-shot demonstrations are retained. Table 3 newly reports qualitative outcomes, including DoorKey correctness after three refinement iterations and successful corrections following human feedback; these are additional findings, not improved benchmark scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.5 introduces a sparse-task formalization, Proposition 1 and a proof sketch asserting optimal-policy preservation under nonpositive-cycle and terminal-reward-dominance assumptions. v1 contains definitions and training equations but no corresponding proposition or guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: automated LARM generation, language-mediated skill sharing, broad empirical effectiveness and compositional zero-shot generalization.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 explicitly limits zero-shot generalization to novel compositions within the same domain. Section 2.1 clarifies broader Boolean-predicate applicability, while Appendix A.4 supplies specific explanations of generation failures and human remedies beyond v1's general human-verification caveat.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands disclosure of LARM construction: Section 3 identifies GPT-4o, and Appendix A.4 documents the interactive feedback interface and environment-specific human corrections and reward tuning. Appendix A.10 also supplies entered_goal_room and got_ball implementations omitted from v1's listing. Existing prompts and RL hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds substantive contrasts with L*LM and RAD, and Appendix A.6/Table 4 systematically positions ARM-FM against automata and FM-guided approaches, including MaestroMotif. The previous Exploration survey and associated references are removed, shifting emphasis toward semantic conditioning and demonstration/interface requirements.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise focused explanatory edits, revised related-work paragraphs, three inserted appendix sections, corrected appendix numbering, and updated affiliations and acknowledgements rather than an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into the ICLR template, replacing the colored title block and changing typography, margins, headers, captions and figure placement. Two tables are added, Figures 19–20 now share a page, and Figures 6–7 receive revised baseline legends while retaining their results.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through generator identification and concrete human-intervention disclosures. However, its new Appendix A.5 asserts that all experimental LARMs satisfy the absence-of-positive-cycles condition, while the Meta-World listing in A.9 contains u0->u1->u2->u0 with reward 0.20 + 0.40 - 0.40 = +0.20. This newly introduced theoretical inconsistency offsets clear documentation benefits. With benchmark evidence unchanged, a reliable net quality direction is unclear.
